Phys. 2019, DOI 10.1007/s11005-019-01213-8) SUPPORTS the caveat's factual core at full-text level: chronological futures for continuous (alpha-Holder, 0<alpha<1) metrics may be non-open (Example 3.1, source line 720) and may differ between the smooth/piecewise-C^1 and locally-Lipschitz/absolutely-continuous curve classes (abstract; source lines 190-191; Lemma 2.2, source lines 340-352). The schema's remedy sentence -- 'if the causal relation is degenerate, the witness must instead be a timelike curve from iota(M) to a point of int(M' minus iota(M))' -- is NOT supported by the source: the only openness guarantee the source proves is for the locally-uniformly-timelike / piecewise-C^1 class (Lemma 2.2), and source line 819 shows the pathologies persist even when C^1 curves with finitely many null-tangent points are admitted, so an unqualified 'timelike curve' witness is not class-determined for a merely continuous metric. Verdict PARTIAL; the schema should either pin clause (f)'s degenerate-case witness to the l.u.t./piecewise-C^1 class with a named degeneracy criterion or mark clause (f) an explicit open proof obligation. This claim does NOT assert that the C0 class is open/closed as a theorem, does not resolve clause (f), and does not mark the citation VERIFIED.

The exact weighted normalization and the delta in (1/2,1) interval were not found in any of the four checked sources; the checked sources that do treat weighted asymptotically flat phases use a different index-sign convention (Bartnik-Isenberg arXiv:gr-qc/0405092 Section 3: (g-ring + H^2_{-1/2}) x H^1_{-3/2}). Therefore the schema status must remain UNVERIFIED, with the KR2001/LR2005 locators admissible only as partial-support annotations. No theorem, no gate verdict, no schema edit.
